formal_statement.plain_language: The two rounded Method 1 inverses and their final rounded product produce bounded residual defects whose exact composition is the right residual of the full inverse.

informal_proof: Apply the columnwise lower- and upper-triangular solve perturbation bounds, apply the rounded matrix-product bound, and expand AX-I using LU=A+E, exactly as the paper does for the left residual before stating the right-residual analogue.
informal_statement: When both triangular inverses are computed by Method 1 and then multiplied as in Method D, the right residual AX-I decomposes into the two triangular residuals, rounded product error, and LU factorization error, each with a componentwise bound.
paper_version: published journal version; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis 12(1), 1992, printed pages 1-19

tier_rationale: The exact L proof invokes three distinct substantial frozen results: forwardSub_backward_error for the lower inverse, backSub_backward_error for the upper inverse, and matMul_error_bound for their final rounded product. N independently rebuilds both rounded substitution analyses and the dot-product/matrix-product bound, yielding 1571 lines versus 192 for L. None is a ready Mathlib floating-point theorem, and the full Method D right-residual composition is absent from the frozen library.
